evals.name: engineering-explainer
evals.prompt: Build me a slide deck explaining our new caching layer to the engineering team. Cover: the problem (the Postgres primary gets hammered ~12k reads/sec on hot product pages), the approach (Redis in front, cache-aside with a 30s TTL), a diagram of the request flow (client -> cache -> DB on miss), the results (cache hit rate ~86%, p99 read latency dropped from 215ms to 19ms, DB read load down ~7x), and a short rollout plan. I want it animated and as a single HTML file I can present full-screen.
evals.expected_output: A single self-contained .html deck: title, problem, an animated request-flow diagram (client->cache->DB), a before/after latency comparison, rollout, close. Scales to fit, keyboard/click nav, animations on each slide.

evals.name: doc-to-deck
evals.prompt: Turn the attached incident postmortem into a futuristic, animated presentation I can share with the wider team. Single HTML file, dark theme, a timeline/flow of what happened, and a slide on the fix. Keep it tight, around 6-7 slides.
evals.expected_output: A single .html animated deck derived from the postmortem: title, impact summary, an animated timeline/flow of the incident, root cause, the fix, prevention. Dark/futuristic theme. Facts taken from the doc, not invented.

evals.name: pitch-mobile
evals.prompt: Make a quick pitch deck for a side project of mine: a CLI tool called 'ctxzip' that compresses the context you send to an LLM so you pay fewer tokens. 5-6 slides, dark theme, include a before/after token comparison (about 40k tokens down to 6k) and a small diagram of how it sits between your shell and the model. It needs to look good on my phone too since I'll show people from there.
evals.expected_output: A single .html pitch deck, 5-6 slides, dark theme: hook, problem, how it works (small diagram), before/after token calc, close. Must scale to a phone viewport (responsive canvas). Animated.

evals.name: workshop-one-pager
evals.prompt: Build me a presentation for an internal engineering workshop about our new 'CodeLens' context platform for bug fixing. The audience is senior engineers and delivery managers, so it needs to look like a professional consulting deck — light corporate style, not a flashy dark theme. The key slide must tell the whole story on one slide: (1) current challenges — fragmented context across code/docs/tickets, a huge legacy codebase (~40M LOC across ~60 subsystems), slow manual investigation, weak impact traceability, and results that depend on who does the work; (2) the CodeLens knowledge base in the middle — a source map connecting requirements, specs, code, tests and defect history, plus an impact evidence chain (change -> impacted -> evidence -> decision); (3) the skills it enables — standardized bug analysis, impact analysis, code review support, test case selection; and on the right the outcomes: faster bug resolution, high-quality evidence, consistent delivery, less rework. Finish that slide with a bottom strip showing the progression from manual context hunting to consistent evidence-based delivery. 4-5 slides total: cover, agenda, that big slide, and a closing. Single HTML file, animated.
evals.expected_output: A light corporate deck whose centrepiece is a consulting-style poster slide: numbered red/blue/green stage panels with icon cards, a hub/source-map cluster, an evidence chain, outcome chips with checks, and a bottom progression band. All text legible (>=14px), fits 1280x720, animated per slide.
assertions: Single self-contained HTML deck (no external script src references)
Fixed 1280x720 canvas with the seedable nav engine token var n=slides.length,i=0;
Reveal/diagram animation gated on .slide.active so it replays on revisit
prefers-reduced-motion support block present
Light corporate theme: white/light canvas with a dark navy/blue header band, not a dark neon theme
No SVG diagram text below 14px and no check_diagram.js failures
Numbered stage panels 1-2-3 with semantic tones (red challenge, blue core, green skills)
Central hub/source-map cluster with at least 4 satellite nodes (requirements/specs/code/tests/history)
Evidence chain change -> impacted -> evidence -> decision appears as a small flow
At least 4 outcome cards/chips with check styling on the outcomes side
Full-width bottom progression band (manual hunting -> shared context -> consistent delivery)

evals.name: before-after-kb
evals.prompt: I need slides for a lunch-and-learn pitching our team's knowledge base initiative ('TeamBrain') to management. Professional corporate look, white background — think consulting-firm slides. The centerpiece slide compares life WITHOUT the knowledge base (documents, tickets, source code, chat threads and individual know-how all scattered, nobody knows what's where — results: prompt-dependent output, long onboarding, repeated questions, inconsistent answers) versus WITH TeamBrain (code graph, docs/specs, defect history and standards feeding one unified knowledge base that serves the AI assistant, developers, reviewers and PMs — outcomes: faster onboarding, consistent reviews, less rework). Put a 3-step 'how it learns' column between the two sides: understand -> connect -> contextualize. End the slide with a key takeaway bar. Around 4 slides, single self-contained HTML, animated but tasteful.
evals.expected_output: A light corporate deck with a before/after contrast poster: red 'without' panel with scattered sources, a centre 3-step column, a green 'with' panel where sources converge into a knowledge base and fan out to consumers, outcome chips, and a key-takeaway band.
assertions: Single self-contained HTML deck (no external script src references)
Fixed 1280x720 canvas with the seedable nav engine token var n=slides.length,i=0;
Reveal/diagram animation gated on .slide.active so it replays on revisit
prefers-reduced-motion support block present
Light corporate theme: white/light canvas with a dark navy/blue header band, not a dark neon theme
No SVG diagram text below 14px and no check_diagram.js failures
Side-by-side WITHOUT (red-toned) vs WITH (green-toned) contrast panels on one slide
WITHOUT side shows a scattered-sources motif (dashed/chaotic links or question marks)
Three-step learning column present: understand -> connect -> contextualize
WITH side shows sources converging into a unified knowledge base and fanning out to at least 3 consumer roles
Key takeaway band at the bottom of the comparison slide

evals.name: architecture-pipeline
evals.prompt: Create an animated HTML deck (one file) documenting the architecture of our internal RAG platform 'DocMesh' for an enterprise architecture review board. Corporate, light, dense and precise — think vendor reference-architecture slides. The main slide is the end-to-end architecture in 4 numbered stages: 1) data sources (git repositories, Confluence pages, test cases & defect history, coding standards); 2) ingestion & understanding with two parallel tracks — a document track (preprocessing -> semantic chunking -> entity recognition -> embedding) and a code track (AST parsing -> call-graph extraction -> dependency mapping -> code embedding); 3) the unified knowledge core — a living knowledge graph linking specs, modules, classes, design decisions and business logic; 4) context delivery — an MCP/REST gateway with retrieval & ranking serving agents (IDE assistant, review bot, CI agent, chat assistant). Add a bottom bar covering data privacy, access control, audit/traceability and enterprise readiness. Cover + architecture slide + one 'what it enables' slide + close.
evals.expected_output: A light corporate deck whose main slide is a 4-stage reference architecture: numbered stage columns, two vertical ingestion mini-chains, a knowledge-graph mesh core with labelled entities, a delivery column with gateway and agents, and a bottom compliance strip.
assertions: Single self-contained HTML deck (no external script src references)
Fixed 1280x720 canvas with the seedable nav engine token var n=slides.length,i=0;
Reveal/diagram animation gated on .slide.active so it replays on revisit
prefers-reduced-motion support block present
Light corporate theme: white/light canvas with a dark navy/blue header band, not a dark neon theme
No SVG diagram text below 14px and no check_diagram.js failures
Four numbered architecture stages laid out left-to-right (sources, ingestion, knowledge core, delivery)
Two parallel ingestion mini-chains (document track and code track) with at least 3 steps each
Knowledge core drawn as a graph/mesh with at least 4 labelled entities (spec/module/class/decision/logic)
Delivery stage lists a gateway plus at least 3 consuming agents
Bottom compliance strip covering privacy, access control, audit and enterprise readiness

evals.name: reuse-html-template
evals.prompt: Our team's previous quarterly deck is at <path-to-branded-deck.html> — use it as the template. Same cover style, same header band, same closing slide; don't change our branding. Build a new 4-slide animated deck introducing 'Streamline', our release-readiness workflow: the four gates every release candidate passes (code-freeze checks, full regression suite, security scan, release sign-off), a slide showing how a candidate moves gate to gate with what happens on a failure (back to dev, fix, re-enter), and the outcomes we expect (fewer hotfixes, predictable release dates, auditable go/no-go decisions). Single self-contained HTML file.
evals.expected_output: A new deck whose cover, header band and closing slide are inherited verbatim from the provided template deck (scraped via deck_chrome.py, brand wordmark and band gradient intact, no placeholder branding), with entirely new Streamline content in the body.
assertions: Single self-contained HTML deck (no external script src references)
Fixed 1280x720 canvas with the seedable nav engine token var n=slides.length,i=0;
Cover slide inherited from the template deck's cover (brand wordmark and cover treatment), not newly invented
Header band inherited on body slides with the template's band styling and brand wordmark
Closing slide inherited from the template deck's end slide styling
No placeholder branding from stock templates in the deliverable
New requested content present; the template's old body content not carried over
